Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck
and low back pain and muscle stiffness. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent
with the force and direction of the impact. Over the course of 25 visits, care
consisted of physical therapy, spinal mobilization, therapeutic exercise, and home
exercsie instruction, progressing in a typical pattern with visit frequency tapering
as symptoms improved and range of motion returned. Examination revealed rdeuced
cervical and lumbar range of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness, which support
the reported injury, while neurological screening, reflexes, and strength testing were
within normal limits. The patient reports no prior injury or treatment to the neck or
low back. Billed services reflect single charges for each visit without duplication.
Patient was discharged with a home program and instructed to return if symptoms recur.
Prognosis for full recovery is good.
